epithet: A father’s counsel to his son
lede: A wise man sits with his son and tells him, in ten sentences, how to live: worship none but Allah; nothing you do is hidden, though it be the weight of a mustard seed inside a rock; pray; bear what befalls you; and do not walk the earth as if you owned it.

names.name: Luqmān
names.note: After the sage whose advice to his son it preserves. The majority of the early scholars held that he was a wise and righteous man, not a prophet; the Qurʾan says only that he was given wisdom.

revelation.detail: It is Makkan in the saying of most. Two or three ayat are reported as Madinan — those beginning “If all the trees on earth were pens” (31:27) — from ʿAṭāʾ, Qatādah and, in al-Qurṭubī’s report, Ibn ʿAbbās; and al-Ḥasan excepted the fourth ayah, on the ground that prayer and zakāh were legislated in Madinah. The traditional order places it fifty-seventh.

evidence.quote: سُورَةُ لُقْمانَ وَهِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ في قَوْلِ الأكْثَرِينَ. ورُوِيَ عَنْ عَطاءٍ أنَّهُ قالَ: هي مَكِّيَّةٌ سِوى آيَتَيْنِ مِنها نَزَلَتا بِالمَدِينَةِ

setting: It opens by calling the Qurʾan “the wise Book”, and wisdom is its subject from beginning to end: who has it, and who trades it away.

The one who trades it away comes first. “Among people is one who buys idle talk, to lead astray from the way of Allah without knowledge, and to make a mockery of it.” The commentators relate this to al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, who brought back from his travels the tales of the Persian kings and would gather an audience with them when the Prophet ﷺ recited. Ibn Masʿūd, asked about the “idle talk” of the ayah, swore three times that it is singing.

Then comes the one who has it. Luqmān is not placed among the prophets; he is given as a man to whom Allah gave wisdom, and the first use he makes of it is to bring up his child. His counsel begins with the greatest matter — “My son, do not associate anything with Allah; association is a tremendous wrong” — and moves through accountability, prayer, enjoining right and forbidding wrong, and patience, down to the bearing of the body: do not turn your cheek from people in scorn, do not strut, be moderate in your walk, and lower your voice. When the Companions were distressed by another ayah, about those who mix their faith with wrong, the Prophet ﷺ reassured them with Luqmān’s sentence: it is not as you think; it is association.

In the middle of the father’s speech the surah interrupts, in Allah’s own voice, to speak of parents: the mother who carried her child in weakness upon weakness; gratitude owed to Me and to them; and the limit — if they press you to associate with Me, do not obey, but keep them company in this world with kindness. Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ said that this came down about him and his mother.
It closes with five things whose knowledge Allah has kept to Himself. The Prophet ﷺ called them the keys of the unseen.

occasions.title: “It is not as you think”
occasions.text: When there came down, “Those who believe and do not mix their faith with wrong,” it weighed heavily on the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they said: “Which of us does not wrong himself?” He said: “It is not as you think. It is only what Luqmān said to his son: ‘My son, do not associate anything with Allah; association is a tremendous wrong.’”
occasions.source: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: al-Bukhārī (4776) and Muslim (124).

occasions.title: Saʿd and his mother
occasions.text: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ’s mother swore not to eat or drink until he abandoned his religion, saying that Allah had commanded him to obey his parents. These ayat came down: goodness to parents, and no obedience to them in associating others with Allah.

aim: To bring out the wisdom that accords with the revealed law — with Luqmān given as its example.
themes: The words of Allah are inexhaustible
The five keys of the unseen

outline.title: The wise Book, and the idle tale
outline.summary: Alif Lām Mīm. These are the ayat of the wise Book: guidance and mercy for those who do good. Among people is one who buys idle talk to lead astray from the way of Allah; when Our ayat are recited to him he turns away in pride, as though he had not heard. He created the heavens without pillars that you see, and cast firm mountains into the earth. This is the creation of Allah: so show Me what those besides Him have created.

outline.title: Luqmān’s counsel
outline.summary: We gave Luqmān wisdom: be grateful to Allah. “My son, do not associate anything with Allah.” — And We have enjoined on man concerning his parents: be grateful to Me and to your parents; but if they strive to make you associate with Me, do not obey them. — “My son, though it be the weight of a mustard seed, in a rock or in the heavens or in the earth, Allah will bring it forth. My son, establish the prayer, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and be patient over what befalls you. Do not turn your cheek from people in contempt, nor walk the earth exultantly. Be moderate in your pace and lower your voice.”

outline.title: Favours seen and unseen
outline.summary: Do you not see that Allah has subjected to you what is in the heavens and the earth, and lavished on you His favours, outward and inward? Yet some dispute about Allah without knowledge. When told to follow what Allah has sent down they say, “We follow what we found our fathers upon.” Whoever submits his face to Allah, and does good, has grasped the firmest handhold.

outline.title: The words of Allah
outline.summary: If all the trees on earth were pens, and the sea — with seven more seas to add to it — were ink, the words of Allah would not be exhausted. Your creation and your raising are but as a single soul. Do you not see the ships running on the sea by Allah’s favour? When waves cover them like canopies they call on Allah, sincere to Him in religion; and when He brings them safe to land, some of them are lukewarm.

outline.title: The Day, and the five
outline.summary: O mankind, be mindful of your Lord, and fear a Day when no father can avail his son, nor a son his father. Let not the life of this world deceive you. With Allah is the knowledge of the Hour; He sends down the rain; He knows what is in the wombs. No soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die.

keyAyah.why: The first sentence of the counsel, and the one the Prophet ﷺ quoted to his Companions.

virtues.text: “The keys of the unseen are five, which none knows but Allah.” Then he recited: “With Allah is the knowledge of the Hour; He sends down the rain; He knows what is in the wombs; no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow; and no soul knows in what land it will die.”

before: Al-Rūm closed with a command to be patient. Luqmān gives that same command in a father’s voice, among nine others.
after: Luqmān ends with the knowledge that belongs to Allah alone. Al-Sajdah opens with the Book sent down from Him — “about which there is no doubt.”
